seen.where: LWL scans of Ber.A M 20 (1998 microfilm), https://www.lwl.org/325dig-download/Lesesaal-Digitalisate/C_Adelsarchive/Ber/Ber.A/Ber.A_M%2020/Ber.A_M%2020_NNN.jpg, leaves 008, 009, 010, 011, 012 viewed (also 003, 030 by the sweep)
seen.extent: Leaf 008: about 2 lines of numeric groups (e.g. 143 181 114 190 196 ... 312 ... 216) above a French closing dated Paris 16 April 1801, signed 'le Baron de Reube/Neube' (reading uncertain), mentioning Cobenzl and Lucchesini. Leaf 009: about 9 lines of three-digit groups interleaved with German plaintext lines. Leaf 010 closes that letter, Paris, 2 June 1807. Rest of the 234 images not paged.
seen.cipher: Three-digit numeric groups from a small set (about 25 distinct values, 110-320, with 114, 190, 196, 312, 216 very frequent), i.e. a letter- or syllable-sized number substitution, written in lines that alternate with German plain text on leaf 009 (the German lines are an ordinary covering letter, not an interlinear decipherment). Leaves 011-012 are a plain French report to 'Madame' (Nr. 6, Portugal expedition, so 1807). No decipherment or key sheet written on or with the leaves seen. The file therefore runs at least 1801-1807, not only 1801-02.

2437.unvetted: Leaf 001 and 003 of Cap.C.I S 1199,11 viewed: German salutation + two lines, then about 16-19 lines of 3-4 digit dot-separated groups (300-3100, many with dash/tick marks), no plaintext between, no decipherment on the leaves; verso 002 blank with 'Steinsches Archiv' stamp. But the printed-edition check could not be done: Botzenhart 'Briefwechsel' II (1931), Stein 'Briefe und amtliche Schriften' / 2015 De Gruyter 'Briefwechsel' (section Nov 1808), Pertz and Niebuhr 'Lebensnachrichten' are not online/readable here (web searches x4 found no text, DECODE/Tomokiyo/Lasry no hit). A printed decipherment is plausible, so not promotable until a volume is checked.
